newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Le Pen says defeated Chirac should resign.
newsitem.headline: France's Le Pen says defeated Chirac should resign.

text.p: French extreme-right National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen said on Sunday that President Jacques Chirac had suffered a personal defeat in a parliamentary election won by the left and should resign.

"This is not a defeat, it is a disaster," Le Pen said in a statement. "Jacques Chirac has been beaten twice, in votes on the first round and in seats on the second. He played double or quits and lost. He should draw the consequences and hand his mandate back to the people."

"Behind the misleading appearances, the nation has been weakened, its independence has been weakened, its economic, social and diplomatic forces ruined by plans for Europeanisation. We must change paths, for things can only get worse," Le Pen said.
He appealed to all "healthy parties" to join hands with his National Front in reshaping France's political landscape, "to define and bring about a new politics that is popular, social and national."
Le Pen said he expected only one of his candidates to have won a seat in parliament, as projected by polling firms.
But he said he would convene the Front's political bureau on Monday to plot strategy for a possible reshaping of French politics.
